purpose: Known risks, limitations, provisional states, and upstream blockers for the SDK/CLI/MCP/OpenAPI platform. Every entry needs evidence, mitigation, and a closure gate.

risks.summary: Historical Fern CLI bare-array pagination limitation is no longer an active blocker because the required SDK generator is local; wrapper pagination helpers remain the supported public surface.
risks.impact: No active generator blocker. Generated list methods still need to preserve page/page-size request shapes consumed by iterAll, iterPages, and paginate.
risks.mitigation: Keep pagination wrappers tested and keep local generator comparison/drift checks active.
risks.closureGate: No closure planned; keep as historical evidence unless the pagination helper surface is intentionally redesigned.

risks.summary: The historical Fern addon-token workaround is retired; local generated auth types now model exactly one token mode.
risks.impact: A regression could reintroduce workaround casts or allow callers to send both Clockify auth headers.
risks.mitigation: Keep generated HeaderAuthProvider auth options mutually exclusive and keep createClockifyClient auth tests active.
risks.closureGate: No closure planned; keep discrepancy evidence and SDK auth tests as regression coverage.

risks.summary: Live tests intentionally mutate Clockify state and must run only against a sacrificial sandbox workspace.
risks.impact: Live proof is high value but unsafe against customer workspaces.
risks.mitigation: Require explicit env vars and document sandbox-only usage before running live gates.
risks.closureGate: Keep live proof receipts showing sandbox cleanup; never generalize live gates to customer workspaces.

evidence.contains: Never run live gates against a customer workspace
make perfect-live        Explicit sandbox/live cleanup proof. Requires live env vars.

risks.summary: The approval receipt binds the exact manifest and campaign-receipt hashes, but its approvedBy field is a local operator-process attestation rather than cryptographic identity proof.
risks.impact: Repository write access can author an approval receipt; local validation proves artifact integrity and ordering, not the real-world identity of the approver.
risks.mitigation: Require explicit maintainer approval of both candidate hashes, retain protected-branch review and release-environment controls externally, and never let the campaign generate or import its own approval.
risks.closureGate: No local closure is possible. Close only if approval moves to an authenticated remote signature or protected-environment attestation that binds both artifact hashes.

evidence.contains: process attestation, not cryptographic identity proof

risks.summary: Packages are published to npm under the unofficial @apet97 scope; publication stays tag-gated CI, so npm publication is not the default path for routine changes and the publish manifest fields + prepublishOnly gates remain load-bearing.
risks.impact: Publishing is a deliberate tag push (wrapper-v*/cli-v*/mcp-v*); the prepublishOnly gates and tag-vs-version guards are the safety rails. Re-publishing on every change is not the workflow.
risks.mitigation: Keep release/support policy, package contract, and CI contract aligned with the tag-gated publish stance.
risks.closureGate: Only publish after explicit maintainer approval plus perfect-full, pack-smoke, and release/support proof.

evidence.contains: npm publication is not the default path

risks.summary: Tag-triggered npm release workflows publish all three packages on prefixed tags (wrapper-v*/cli-v*/mcp-v*); the maintainer reviewed and enabled them (release.yml/ci-cli-release.yml/ci-mcp-release.yml each publish on a tag whose version matches its package.json). Version bumps are hand-cut, not automated.
risks.impact: Release automation still requires explicit maintainer approval per publish; local packable readiness is not the same as permission to publish. The tag-vs-version guard remains load-bearing.
risks.mitigation: Keep the no-default-publish policy, package contracts, CI contract, and release-decision planner visible; do not run or modify release automation casually. Bump versions by hand through the documented cascade, then push the prefixed tag.
risks.closureGate: Maintainer reviewed release.yml + release-please.yml on 2026-05-28; on 2026-06-28 the maintainer enabled tag-triggered npm publish for all three packages under the unofficial @apet97 scope (CLI/MCP scaffolds flipped from inert to cli-v*/mcp-v* publishers; SDK moved from bare v* to wrapper-v* tags). On 2026-07-27 release-please.yml was retired: it anchored on the 2026-07-14 releases, ignored `.release-please-manifest.json`, and every PR it filed proposed a version *below* what was already published (last: 0.13.0 -> 0.12.1). `check-ci-contract.mjs` now fails if the workflow returns. The tag-vs-version guard remains load-bearing.

risks.summary: Generated code is a replaceable lower layer, not the product surface users should depend on directly.
risks.impact: Direct imports from generated internals make generator replacement and OpenAPI regeneration brittle.
risks.mitigation: Keep generated-edit, generator-independence, dependency-boundary, and SDK public API gates active.
risks.closureGate: No closure planned; this is a permanent architecture constraint.

risks.summary: The shared offline URL guard rejects non-HTTPS callbacks, embedded credentials, internal hostnames, and non-global or special-purpose IP literals across SDK, CLI, and MCP, but it does not resolve hostnames and therefore cannot defend against DNS rebinding.
risks.impact: A hostname can pass the offline syntax check and later resolve to a private address when Clockify delivers the webhook.
risks.mitigation: Keep literal-host classification aligned with the IANA special-purpose registries, share the validator across all three surfaces, and state the no-DNS-resolution boundary wherever callback safety is documented.
risks.closureGate: No closure planned; this is an accepted limitation of an offline guard. Re-evaluate only if registration gains a request-time host-resolution check.

evidence.contains: DNS rebinding is an accepted limitation

risks.summary: Live read-only proof established that the expense route ignores start/end while honoring pagination; SDK, CLI, and MCP now share one bounded client-side filter contract.
risks.impact: Date-filtered reads can require multiple API pages and may stop at the configured bound, so consumers must inspect the warning and continuation metadata.
risks.mitigation: Keep listExpensesFiltered shared across CLI/MCP, preserve the typed double-nested envelope, and retain the bounded scan plus client-side warning.
risks.closureGate: Closed 2026-07-19 by the sanitized Task 2 live receipt, focused wrapper/CLI/MCP tests, consumer-cast budget, operation-parity drift, and contract gates.

risks.summary: The canonical and generated expense-update multipart request now keeps file optional while preserving the existing expense-create contract.
risks.impact: Scalar updates compile without an unsafe request cast, while callers that supply a receipt still emit one binary file part.
risks.mitigation: Keep the upstream create-vs-update schema regression, downstream generated-type compile proof, exact multipart wire tests, and cast-budget gate active.
risks.closureGate: Closed 2026-07-19 by the Task 3 sanitized receipt, upstream OpenAPI drift/tool gates, downstream codegen and multipart tests, cast removal, consumer-cast budget, risk-register, and contract gates.

evidence.contains: accepts a typed scalar update and emits no file part

risks.summary: The aggregate `all` Mutation workflow run covers wrapper, MCP, and CLI with the exact three report paths and every current global/module floor; the remote-mutation proof risk remains accepted and non-blocking.
risks.impact: The three package scopes now have one authoritative aggregate GitHub proof. Natural artifact expiry only prevents a fresh download; it does not reverse this sanitized recorded verification.
risks.mitigation: Use only the manual GitHub Mutation workflow for mutation proof; do not run local Stryker or a mutation package command.
risks.closureGate: Accepted 2026-07-22 after `make mutation-ci` and the aggregate GitHub Actions run/artifact verification. A new release decision that needs a fresh download dispatches and verifies a new aggregate run.

risks.summary: CI has no GOCLMCP sibling checkout, so scripts/generate-operation-parity.mjs falls back to carrying forward the goMcp values already committed in docs/operation-parity.json instead of re-deriving them from the sibling's tool catalog.
risks.impact: Without a freshness signal, the carried-forward goMcp values could go stale indefinitely if no maintainer regenerates the artifact with the sibling checked out.
risks.mitigation: sources.goMcp on the parity artifact records catalogPresent, carriedForward, and carriedFromVerifiedAt (propagated across repeated sibling-less runs, not reset); a console.warn reports the carried-forward age on every sibling-less regeneration; check-operation-coverage.mjs hard-fails past a 90-day freshness window, but only in the release-proof tier (operation-coverage-run, reached via release-proof/heavy-proof/perfect-full) -- never contract-gates, which is sibling-less by design and must stay green on a fresh carry-forward.
risks.closureGate: No closure planned; this is a permanent architecture constraint of running CI without the sibling repository. Re-evaluate only if the sibling tool catalog becomes fetchable in CI.
